nations.name: Chickahominy Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the Chickahominy River area and Chickahominy Ridge in Virginia, as described in the Tribe's history

facts.text: The Chickahominy Indian Tribe's history describes permanent villages along the Virginia river that still bears its name.
facts.evidence: permanent villages along the Virginia river that still bears our name

facts.text: The Tribe's history says the Treaty of 1646 displaced Chickahominy people from their river homelands.
facts.evidence: The Treaty of 1646 displaced the Chickahominy people

facts.text: The Tribe dates the establishment of Samaria Indian Baptist Church, a community institution, to 1901.
facts.evidence: In 1901, the Chickahominy Tribe established Samaria Indian Baptist Church

facts.text: The Tribe's history describes members building schools and funding teachers' salaries under Virginia's discriminatory education policies.
facts.evidence: tribal members built schools and raised funds

nations.name: Chickahominy Indian Tribe - Eastern Division
nations.lands: New Kent County, Virginia; the Tribe describes roots in Virginia before English colonization

facts.text: The Tribe's history dates the start of its New Kent County school to 1910; the one-room school taught grades 1 through 8.
facts.evidence: A school was started in New Kent County

facts.text: The Tribe's history dates the formation of its own tribal government to 1920 to 1921.
facts.evidence: began forming their own tribal government

facts.text: The Tribe's timeline records a certificate of incorporation for the Chickahominy Indians Eastern Division in 1925.
facts.evidence: A certificate of incorporation was issued

facts.text: In its food-sovereignty account, CIT-ED says a 2022 EPA grant supported a community compost and gardening program.
facts.evidence: develop a community compost and gardening program
